extracted_claims.text: Under the AI Act as originally adopted (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), the obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III (Chapter III, Sections 1-3) were set to apply from 2 August 2026, under Article 113.

The European Parliament's general description (undated, pre-Omnibus) stated high-risk system obligations would become applicable 36 months after entry into force, i.e. around August 2027, differing from the 24-month/2 August 2026 date used elsewhere.
The 'AI Omnibus' / Digital Omnibus on AI amended Article 113 so that the obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III now apply from 2 December 2027.

The obligations for high-risk AI systems that are classified as high-risk because they are embedded in products covered by Union harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I will apply from 2 August 2028.
One source states the extended transition for high-risk AI embedded in regulated products runs only until 2 August 2027, rather than 2 August 2028.
The AI Omnibus Regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026.
Political agreement between the Council and the European Parliament on the AI Omnibus (including the extended high-risk timeline) was reached on 7 May 2026.
The Commission's Digital Package on Simplification ('AI Omnibus') legislative proposal was adopted on 19 November 2025, prior to the political agreement and entry into force of the final regulation.

Before the Omnibus amendments were finalized, commentators noted that if the proposed delay was not approved and enacted before 2 August 2026, the Annex III high-risk obligations would, as a legal default, apply from that date ('backstop').

2 December 2027 is also the date given by Article 113(c)(i) of the consolidated/amended Regulation text for the application of Chapter III, Sections 1-3 (Annex III high-risk systems), excluding Article 6(5).

The consolidated EUR-Lex text (version applicable 27 July 2026) still contains language referencing a 'date of application of Chapter III referred to in Article 113' for legacy high-risk systems placed on the market before that date, without repeating the specific calendar date in the excerpt shown.

The AI Act Service Desk's Article 111 guidance states this provision applies to operators of high-risk AI systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026, referencing that date as the relevant application date for related transitional rules.
A news/blog source claims Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 is the specific instrument that sets 2 December 2027 as the Annex III/Article 6(2) high-risk application date.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act's original text set 2 August 2026 as the application date for high-risk AI system obligations under Annex III (medium confidence), but this deadline has since been superseded. A legislative amendment known as the "AI Omnibus" Regulation, which entered into force on 27 July 2026, has pushed the Annex III compliance date back to **2 December 2027** (high confidence). A separate, later deadline of 2 August 2028 applies to high-risk systems embedded in products covered by Union harmonisation legislation (Annex I), though this is contested by at least one source (low confidence).

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (As Adopted)
Under the AI Act as originally adopted (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), Article 113 set 2 August 2026 as the date when obligations for Annex III high-risk AI systems (Chapter III, Sections 1-3) would become applicable (medium confidence) ([AI Act Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113), [Squire Patton Boggs](https://www.squirepattonboggs.com/media/h3pcmbj2/ai-timeline-implementation-and-compliance.pdf)). A separate, undated European Parliament summary instead described a 36-month timeline (around August 2027), diverging from this figure, likely reflecting an early or outdated draft summary (medium confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence)).

### The AI Omnibus Amendment
The "AI Omnibus" (Digital Omnibus on AI) amended Article 113, delaying the Annex III application date to **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy: AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). This new date is corroborated across multiple EU guidance pages and legal-analysis sources ([Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113), [AnnexOps guide](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)).

The legislative path to this amendment involved several stages: the Commission's Digital Package on Simplification ("AI Omnibus") proposal was adopted on 19 November 2025 (medium confidence) ([Digital Strategy regulatory framework](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)); political agreement between the Council and Parliament was reached on 7 May 2026 (high confidence) ([Council press release](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)); and the Omnibus Regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026 (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [Questa AI](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2026)).

Before this amendment was finalized, commentators noted that absent timely approval, the original 2 August 2026 deadline would apply as a legal "backstop" (low confidence) ([LinkedIn/Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)). One low-confidence source attributes the 2 December 2027 date specifically to a separate instrument, "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744" (low confidence) ([AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027), [EU AI Compass](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)), though this is not corroborated elsewhere.

### Related Transitional Dates
Obligations for high-risk AI systems classified as high-risk because they are embedded in products covered by Union harmonisation legislation (Annex I) will apply from **2 August 2028** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). One source instead states this transition runs only until 2 August 2027 (low confidence) ([Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act)), conflicting with the majority view.

The AI Act Service Desk's Article 111 guidance references 2 August 2026 as the relevant date for AI systems placed on the market before that threshold, for purposes of certain transitional provisions (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Article 111](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
- **Primary contradiction**: Several undated/outdated compliance sources continue to cite 2 August 2026 as the operative Annex III deadline, conflicting with official EU guidance confirming the Omnibus-amended 2 December 2027 date ([Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance) vs. [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). This likely reflects publication before the Omnibus entered into force.
- **Annex I transition date conflict (low confidence)**: Sources disagree on whether the product-embedded high-risk transition extends to 2027 or 2028 ([Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act)).
- **Attribution uncertainty (low confidence)**: The claim that "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744" is the specific instrument setting the 2027 date is low confidence and uncorroborated ([AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)).
- A European Parliament summary's 36-month timeline is inconsistent with the 24-month original Article 113 date, likely due to being an early/outdated draft (medium confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence)).
- The "backstop" framing of the original 2 August 2026 date is itself low confidence and was only a commentator's interpretation prior to the Omnibus's finalization ([LinkedIn/Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)).

## Knowledge Gaps
- Whether 2 December 2027 applies uniformly across all of Chapter III, Sections 1-3, or only to specific sub-provisions, remains only partially clarified.
- The precise legal instrument/name formally enacting the Omnibus amendment is not fully reconciled across sources.
- Whether the 2 August 2026 "backstop" date is explicitly superseded in the full consolidated EUR-Lex text is unconfirmed due to incomplete source excerpts.
- The discrepancy regarding the Annex I product-embedded transition date (2027 vs. 2028) remains unresolved.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act's original text set 2 August 2026 as the application date for high-risk AI system obligations under Annex III (high confidence), but this deadline has since been superseded. A legislative amendment known as the "AI Omnibus" Regulation, which entered into force on 27 July 2026, has pushed the Annex III compliance date back to **2 December 2027** (high confidence). A separate, later deadline of 2 August 2028 applies to high-risk systems embedded in products covered by Union harmonisation legislation (Annex I), though this is contested by at least one source.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline (As Adopted)
Under the AI Act as originally adopted (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), Article 113 set 2 August 2026 as the date when obligations for Annex III high-risk AI systems (Chapter III, Sections 1-3) would become applicable (medium confidence) ([AI Act Implementation Timeline](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113), [Squire Patton Boggs](https://www.squirepattonboggs.com/media/h3pcmbj2/ai-timeline-implementation-and-compliance.pdf)). A separate, undated European Parliament summary instead described a 36-month timeline (around August 2027), diverging from this figure, likely reflecting an early or outdated draft summary (medium confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence)).

### The AI Omnibus Amendment
The "AI Omnibus" (Digital Omnibus on AI) amended Article 113, delaying the Annex III application date to **2 December 2027** (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex consolidated text](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy: AI Omnibus enters into force](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). This new date is corroborated across multiple EU guidance pages and legal-analysis sources ([Art. 113 AI Act](https://ai-act-law.eu/article/113), [AnnexOps guide](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)).

The legislative path to this amendment involved several stages: the Commission's Digital Package on Simplification ("AI Omnibus") proposal was adopted on 19 November 2025 (medium confidence) ([Digital Strategy regulatory framework](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)); political agreement between the Council and Parliament was reached on 7 May 2026 (high confidence) ([Council press release](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)); and the Omnibus Regulation entered into force on 27 July 2026 (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [Questa AI](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2026)).

Before this amendment was finalized, commentators noted that absent timely approval, the original 2 August 2026 deadline would apply as a legal "backstop" (low confidence) ([LinkedIn/Oliver Patel](https://www.linkedin.com/posts/oliver-patel_when-will-eu-ai-act-high-risk-ai-compliance-activity-7401984085377830912-RglO)). One low-confidence source attributes the 2 December 2027 date specifically to a separate instrument, "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744" (low confidence) ([AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027), [EU AI Compass](https://euaicompass.com/timeline.html)), though this is not corroborated elsewhere.

### Related Transitional Dates
Obligations for high-risk AI systems classified as high-risk because they are embedded in products covered by Union harmonisation legislation (Annex I) will apply from **2 August 2028** (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk FAQ](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). One source instead states this transition runs only until 2 August 2027 (low confidence) ([Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act)), conflicting with the majority view.

The AI Act Service Desk's Article 111 guidance references 2 August 2026 as the relevant date for AI systems placed on the market before that threshold, for purposes of certain transitional provisions (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk, Article 111](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
- **Primary contradiction**: Several undated/outdated compliance sources continue to cite 2 August 2026 as the operative Annex III deadline, conflicting with official EU guidance confirming the Omnibus-amended 2 December 2027 date ([Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance) vs. [Digital Strategy](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). This likely reflects publication before the Omnibus entered into force.
- **Annex I transition date conflict**: Sources disagree on whether the product-embedded high-risk transition extends to 2027 or 2028 (low confidence claim flagged) ([Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act)).
- **Attribution uncertainty**: The claim that "Regulation (EU) 2026/1744" is the specific instrument setting the 2027 date is low confidence and uncorroborated ([AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)).
- A European Parliament summary's 36-month timeline is inconsistent with the 24-month original Article 113 date, likely due to being an early/outdated draft (medium confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence)).

## Knowledge Gaps
- Whether 2 December 2027 applies uniformly across all of Chapter III, Sections 1-3, or only to specific sub-provisions, remains only partially clarified.
- The precise legal instrument/name formally enacting the Omnibus amendment is not fully reconciled across sources.
- Whether the 2 August 2026 "backstop" date is explicitly superseded in the full consolidated EUR-Lex text is unconfirmed due to incomplete source excerpts.
- The discrepancy regarding the Annex I product-embedded transition date (2027 vs. 2028) remains unresolved.
